title: Harrier customer implementation — personal play notes
body:
Quick personal scratchpad for Harrier implementation — capture of action items, quick commands, gotchas. Not a final runbook; cleaning up later for SE handoff.

Context:
- Customer: Harrier (edge retail analytics) — must run in their VPC (AWS us-west-2).
- Scope: Private deployment (control plane with customer VPC peering), dedicated GPU nodes for low-latency POS use-cases, model pinning to open models, KMS integration for keys.
- SLA ask: p95 < 120ms for short inference (<= 128 tokens), throughput bursts up to 200 req/s.

Daily log (notes-to-self):
2026-03-09 09:20 — Kickoff with Harrier infra team. They prefer tag-based routing and strict egress rules. Need IAM role for us (infra-redwood-deploy).
2026-03-10 14:05 — Confirmed VPC CIDR: 10.40.0.0/16. Ask SRE to reserve 10.40.10.0/24 for Redwood nodes.
2026-03-11 08:40 — HSM/KMS details: they use AWS CloudHSM cluster (dev-2). Must test key rotations w/o downtime.
2026-03-12 11:55 — Run quick perf test with opt-2.7B-8bit variant; baseline p95 ~= 95ms on a g4dn-equivalent; good but memory margins tight when KV cache size = 4GB.

Top TODOs (ordered):
- [ ] Prep VPC peering config snippet for Harrier networking team (include route tables, SGs) — target 2026-03-13.
- [ ] Create sealed-secret template for KMS/HSM integration and pass to security review.
- [ ] Validate model fallback policy: primary redwood/opt-2.7b-8bit, fallback redwood/opt-1.3b-int8 with automatic session migration.
- [ ] Canary plan: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 48h if error rate < 0.5% and token-cost within 10% of expected.
- [ ] Add test prompt set (retail queries + adversarial strings) to eval harness; link HAR-1123.

Networking notes (quick commands/snippets):
- Ask customer to open outbound to our control-plane endpoints: cp-usw2.redwood.ai:443 and allow inbound from cp node IPs for management (list will be provided).
- Route table example (send to Harrier):
  - Destination: 172.31.0.0/16 -> Target: peering-conn-0abcd
  - Destination: 10.40.10.0/24 -> Target: eni-redwood-nodes
- Security groups: allow TCP 443 from customer admin CIDR, allow node-to-node on 50051–50060 for internal rpc (we use gPRC range), allow redis on 6379 only from node SG.

Runtime/config decisions noted:
- Model variants: pin primary to redwood/opt-2.7b-8bit (customer asked for 2.7B), keep smaller 1.3B int8 for fallback to reduce cost during capacity pressure.
- KV cache: start with 4GB per node (tune after first week). If memory pressure observed, enable prefix-only caching for longest 512 token prefixes.
- Batching: configure adaptive batching with max latency target 40ms; prefer size-bound mode for POS (steady short requests).
- Quantization profile: test 8-bit dynamic; avoid int4 until we validate hallucination/regression on eval set.

Quick troubleshooting TODOs (notes from yesterday's run):
- When we saw OOM on node-3: swapbed logs showed high ephemeral disk use from KV snapshots. Fix by increasing ephemeral disk to 200GB for now.
- Observed intermittent 502s when canary routing changed — suspected race in autoretry policy. Patch in infra PR 984 to add graceful drain window.

Test prompts (copy these into eval harness):
1) "Summarize transaction 2026-03-11 for store 053: list anomalies, flagged items." (expected: 3 bullets, mention refund anomaly)
2) "Given receipt TL-987, extract SKU, total, timestamp in JSON." (structured output test)
3) Adversarial: long malformed input with repeated tokens — ensure generation truncates and returns error code 413 with helpful message.

Rollout/checklist (fast checklist to follow during deploy):
- Pre-deploy:
  - [ ] Confirm VPC peering (Harrier + Redwood).
  - [ ] Keys provisioned in CloudHSM and tested with dev cluster.
  - [ ] Control-plane IP allowlist shared with Harrier security.
  - [ ] Canary traffic routing configured (1% traffic).
- Deploy day:
  - [ ] Deploy primary model to 2 nodes, start canary at 1% for 2h, run smoke tests (p95, error rate, token-cost).
  - [ ] If smoke pass, scale canary to 5% for 6h, monitor eval harness.
  - [ ] Monitor disk/memory and KV cache hit rate (goal >= 35%).
- Post-deploy:
  - [ ] Schedule 1-week retrospective with Harrier eng to tune batching/quantization.

Notes-to-self (random):
- Keep a short list of troubleshooting one-liners for SRE pager:
  - Check kv cache hit: curl -s http://localhost:9090/metrics | grep kv_cache_hit_ratio
  - Drain node gracefully: curl -X POST http://cp.local/drain?node=node-3
  - Re-seed model from snapshot: redwoodctl model restore --model opt-2.7b --snapshot s2026-03-10

Open questions / follow-ups to ask Harrier:
- Are there IP ranges that will change frequently (we want stable allowlist)?
- Expected peak QPS window (they mentioned "lunch rush" but need exact hours).
- Any regulatory constraints on token logging/retention for PII? If yes, enable redact pipeline and longer KMS retention policies.

Later cleanup items (for formal runbook):
- Convert this scratchpad into a runbook page under confluence: "Harrier — Private Deployment Runbook".
- Move test prompts to eval repo and tag with HAR-1123.
- Draft customer-facing FAQ about model fallback behavior and cost implications.

End of scratchpad — will tidy and share with Omar/Priya before handing to solutions-eng docs owner.
